rationale: The sample size calculation shows that a definitive trial at this hospital would take nearly five years, and the retrieved pilot trial failed on outcome completeness because ward values were not documented (c2). First-on-the-list scheduling cannot be relied on in orthopaedics (c3). A single-site feasibility study of the protocol, with pre-specified progression criteria, answers the questions that decide whether a multicentre trial is worth running, and the dose plan evidence (c1) justifies testing the protocol at all.
alternatives: Definitive two-arm randomised trial at this hospital (refused: about 342 participants would take nearly five years)
Multicentre definitive trial now (refused: no data yet on delivery, recruitment or outcome completeness)
Randomised pilot trial (refused for now: the key uncertainties are delivery and documentation, which a single-arm study can measure with fewer patients)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for pilot and feasibility trials (applicable items)
whyNotMoreComplex: Randomising within a feasibility study would halve the patients receiving the protocol without answering the delivery questions any better.

decision.statement: Replace the definitive trial with a nine-month single-site feasibility study of the protocol, with progression criteria for recruitment (at least 50 percent of eligible patients), protocol delivery (dose table and nurse call for at least 80 percent) and outcome completeness (at least 90 percent), before any randomised trial.
decision.question: How should the hospital evaluate the perioperative glucose protocol, given the recruitment it can achieve?

criteria.text: Outcome completeness and recruitment, not effect, are the main uncertainties for a trial at this hospital.
Scheduling cannot be delivered for orthopaedic patients, so the protocol must be shown to work without it.

gates.evidence: Departmental grant DRG-2026-09 of 12,000 awarded on 2026-08-30, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Multicentre definitive trial after the feasibility study
decision.note: Rests on claims c1 to c3 and on the stats stage's sample size; replaces the accepted trial decision.

summary: Feasibility study recommended in place of the trial; the second decision is proposed.
